title: What each official sponsored and carried
question: Which Board files carry each supervisor’s or mayor’s name, what kind are they, and how much money do their titles name?
finding: 6,984 Board files name a sponsor: 6,168 of the 10,373 introduced since 2019, and 816 of the 6,507 introduced from 2014 to 2018, where the record on disk carries sponsors almost only for money and land-use files (760 of those 816). Rafael Mandelman is named on the most (2,368). Of the 997 sponsored contracts, grant agreements, leases and loans, 283 (28.4%) carry the Mayor as sponsor: London N. Breed 167 files naming $4.05 billion; Daniel Lurie 59 files naming $1.25 billion; Edwin Lee 51 files naming $805.3 million. District add-back lines add $71.3 million across 1,025 lines. The final Board roll call is on disk for 1,926 of the 2,128 sponsored money files (appropriations and grants the City accepts included): 85 drew at least one no vote and 1 failed. A supervisor who sponsored a money file sat on the committee that sent it to the Board in 918 of 2,130 cases (43.1%); the same supervisors’ share of committee seats on all money files sent on in those years would give about 813 (38.2%): more than chance would produce.
how: Sponsors are read from the Board’s legislation record: the list printed on each file’s page, which is on disk for every file introduced from 2019 and, for earlier years, for the money files and land-use files whose pages were fetched; the index of enacted ordinances from 2018 adds a few. “Mayor” as a sponsor is assigned to the person who was Mayor on the day of introduction, from the dates on Form 700 statements. Kinds come from this project’s table of Board money files (contract, grant agreement, lease or property, loan, settlement, grant the City accepts), from titles beginning “Appropriation”, and from the list of land-use matters; everything else is “other”. “Dollars in titles” adds the amount each contract, grant agreement, lease or loan title names (the amount after an amendment). Add-backs are first-year lines of the Board’s June budget lists whose district column names exactly one district, assigned to the supervisor casting roll-call votes for that district on 30 June of that year. The vote columns use the Board’s roll calls on money files, 2015 to 2026, through the shared roll-call reader: the final vote is the last Board passage roll call of the file, and a no vote is any member printed “No” on it. A file was “sent on by a committee” when a committee roll call recommended it or referred it without recommendation; the sponsor “sat on that committee” when the committee’s vote grid lists the sponsor, whatever vote is printed. The comparison is the sponsor’s share of committee seats: of all money files sent on by any committee in the same calendar year while the sponsor was on the Board, the share sent on by a committee whose grid lists the sponsor; the two are compared by drawing each case ten thousand times at that share.
limits: Being connected is not being corrupt, and sponsoring is not deciding: a contract or grant file is an agreement between a City department and the named party, and 28.4% of the sponsored ones carry the Mayor’s name rather than a supervisor’s. Before 2019 the record on disk carries sponsors only for money and land-use files, so officials who left before 2019 show fewer files than they sponsored. A co-sponsored file is counted for every sponsor. Add-back lists name a district, not a supervisor; 117 of 1,142 district lines fall in a year with no seat-holder on the roll call (mostly June 2014). Amounts in titles are ceilings, not payments. Most money files pass without a no vote, and a unanimous vote says nothing about one member. A sponsor sitting on the committee that hears the file is ordinary: files go to the committee for their subject, a supervisor sponsors files in the field of their own committee, and the Budget chair carries the budget; the Mayor, who sponsors the most money files, sits on no committee. For 332 roll calls the Clerk’s vote page says “by the following vote” and lists no member, 306 of them dated 2016-04-13 to 2016-07-26; 315 were read instead from the vote lines in the Clerk’s published minutes of the same meeting, and 17 remain without member votes and are counted nowhere here. Amounts, parties and dates taken from Board file titles are read by machine: in a hand check of 50 titles, 11 had at least one field read wrongly (4 after later fixes).
